subject: The u16 entity id at entity+174h: the two handle tables that own it, the allocation and release rules, the backslash-path entity lookup 009251F0, and the Cloud scene creator's field writes.
headline: The id is a slot index into one of two fixed-size handle tables, not a counter. 00927940 builds table A at 00F89A08 over ids [0, a) and table B at 00F89A5C over [a, a+b), so every reader selects with a single `id < A.count` test. 009517C0's second argument is a requested id, not a flag: zero pops the free list's tail, non-zero takes that exact slot. 009516D0 releases from the entity destructor 009287B0. The per-party lookup 009251F0 matches a case-insensitive backslash path, not a party:name pair. Neither Cloud creator writes +174h, a class pointer or a party field.

fields.field: free slot count = count-1 at construction

list_layout.shape: an embedded 0x10 terminator node plus the head pointer at +10h; a node's +4h holds the address of the link that points at it, which makes unlink two unconditional stores

fields.field: prev (address of the link pointing here)
u16 id = firstId + index; slot 0 is written as 0 and stays out of every list

allocation_rule: 009517c0: if free==0 rebuild (009517c6); requestedId==0 takes the free list tail and its stored id (009517d4), otherwise slots+(requestedId-first)*10h unchecked (009517dd); store the entity at +0ch, unlink, push at the head of the live list +3ch, free-=1. Ids are fixed to slots, so there is no counter and no wraparound; a fresh table hands out firstId+1 upward and released ids come back at the head, so recycling is FIFO and reserved id firstId is never issued.
release_rule: 009516d0: slots+(id-first)*10h, clear +0ch, unlink, push at the head of the free list +1ch, free+=1. Sole caller 00928810 in the destructor 009287b0, which picks the table from the id itself (009287f5 CMP ECX,[00f89a10]).
qualified_name_grammar: component '\\' component ... '\\' leaf, case-insensitive, each component matched in full. 009251f0 first compares the whole remaining string with the node name through 00438e10; on a miss it requires children, a '\\' in the name (00925237 PUSH 0x5c), strlen(nodeName) == prefix length (00925263) and __strnicmp(name, nodeName, prefixLen)==0 (00925273) before recursing into every child with the remainder. No ':' or '@' form exists in the routine.

uncertainties: The two table capacities are unknown: 00927940 has no caller in the image, so only the contiguity of the ranges is established.

00951720 tests slot i (00951737) but relinks slot i-firstId (00951741). Identical for the low table (firstId 0); for the high table it relinks the wrong slot and below i==firstId it addresses memory before the array. Recorded as an original defect, provisional: the path needs an exhausted table and no run-time evidence was collected.
004e9e40 resolves the class name twice and drops the first result (004e9ea2 vs 004e9eeb). The single resolve in the register pass suggests a lazy load followed by a fetch, but neither body proves it.
The vtable+10h name getter used by 009251f0 was read only as a slot value (00cfc3d0+10h = 0042e950, no Ghidra function), so its return is inferred from its use.
The 24 inline copies of the id resolve (xrefs of 00f89a10) were not read; only 00521e30 was.
tooling_problems: `bsp.py ghidra disasm` refuses an address with no function and `disasm-raw` does not exist in this checkout, so the three creator bodies were decoded locally: `bsp.py ghidra bytes` plus capstone in local/disasm_raw.py. mcp__ghidra__disassemble_bytes returns only a byte count, and its non-dry form would mutate the program, so it was not used beyond a dry run.
`bsp.py find EntityId` returns nothing even though kEntityIdOffset and kUnitEntityIdRegistryPrimary exist in the headers; the ledger name search does not cover reconstruction identifiers.

reconstruction.notes: The tables are index-based; the native 'pointer to the link that points at me' in a slot's +4h is a modelling detail, not a layout claim, so the projection carries an in_live_list flag the native derives from its pointers. Where the native computes an unchecked address (009517dd, 009516d5, the sweep's biased index) the projection fails or skips instead, each commented with the diverging instruction. No offset or type name is redeclared: kUnitLayoutOffEntityId and kUnitInstanceNameLengthOffset stay where they are.
